reason: The text describes the daughters of the Midianite priest being driven away by shepherds while performing their duty to water their father's flock. Their suffering (being expelled from the well) is presented as an unprovoked action by the shepherds, not as a consequence of any wrongdoing by the daughters. They are portrayed as victims requiring rescue by Moses, not as people responsible for bringing misfortune upon themselves. No moral or behavioral fault is indicated on their part.
